discussion_comments.comment_body:
Confirmed, and this is real — but I believe it belongs in a separate fix rather than this one.

It is pre-existing and not introduced here. `handle_workspace_close` has the identical gap: `close_selected_workspace()` expands `close_indices` to every member of a non-linked worktree parent's group, while the handler emits a single `workspace.closed` for the targeted workspace only. `handle_pane_close` inherits it too. This PR reuses that same machinery, so it makes the behaviour reachable from `tab.close` without changing it.

Fixing it only in this branch would make `tab.close` and `workspace.close` disagree about how many events a group closure produces, which seems worse than the current consistent-but-incomplete behaviour. A correct fix means having `close_selected_workspace()` report which workspaces it actually removed, then emitting one `workspace.closed` per removal at all three call sites — a change to shared runtime behaviour and its event contract, beyond the focused bug fix intake allows me here.

Worth noting the reachability is narrow: the guard immediately above returns `confirmation_required` whenever `confirm_close` is enabled, which is the default. The gap only opens for users who have explicitly set `confirm_close = false`.

I flagged this in the PR description rather than leaving it implicit. Happy to open a follow-up covering all three call sites if a maintainer wants it.

This is a known, documented limitation of the injection-based approach rather than a new regression, so leaving it as-is for now. The doc comment on `InputSourceRestore` already calls it out: `SendInput` always targets the foreground input queue and cannot address a specific HWND, so if focus moves before restore, the toggle lands on whatever is focused. The macOS input-source path has the same cross-app caveat, and prefix mode is short-lived so in practice the herdr terminal is still focused. A robust fix would require abandoning `SendInput` (e.g. per-window `PostMessage(WM_KEYDOWN)`, which is unreliable for IME state), so it is out of scope for this PR.
